_why: Adjudicated figure picks for questions the one-region rule cannot resolve. It is right for 39 of 41 groups, so it is NOT loosened; these two state a source outright, the way scripts/ppt/extract_figures.py handles the figure its rules get wrong at both ends. Each pick names WHICH paper and page to read, and how to combine that page's regions. Verified by rendering the page and looking at it - the note records what was seen.
_modes: union = union every figure-sized region on that page (correct only where ONE question owns them all - never assume it; 2025-65-2-2 p6 carries TWO questions' figures and would merge them).  ms = read the figure from the MARKING SCHEME instead of the question paper, locating it by question number; 'band' then trims the result to a fractional y-range because the scheme rasterises the whole question block, text included. Every band below was set by rendering it and looking - the first attempt at a0d77754 clipped its own x-axis tick labels.  padTop = extend the crop UPWARDS by N points to take in a caption, which is page text and therefore outside every image region; it replaces PAD on the top edge instead of adding to it, so measure the gap off the page and pass it as measured.

a785d7fad8031e605c63bb637151b15750d2302e.note: Q5 'The graph of a trigonometric function is as shown. Which of the following will represent graph of its inverse?' - the STEM is a graph AND all four options are graphs, so the question is one visual block: stem 354x192, then option C 134x102 and option D 134x79 side by side (A and B fall inside the stem region's band). All three series print the identical layout, so any of them would do; 65-1-2 is named to keep the pick reproducible. Q5 owns every figure on this page, which is what makes union safe here.

71db4a732d1d29a81431a89b0d723c3c44ef1cf5.note: Q16/Q6/Q14 'which of the following depicts the correct relation between set A and B?' - the four options are printed as bare Venn diagrams in a 2x2 grid of 56x56 boxes and nothing else. 65-2-3 is named DELIBERATELY: on 65-2-1 and 65-2-2 the same four boxes share their page with the area-under-a-curve graph of the NEXT question, so union there would splice two questions together. On 65-2-3 p10 the four boxes are the only regions, so union is exactly the option block. (The transcription also describes each option in words, so the row is answerable without the figure; the crop shows the question as actually printed.)

555f13c3d57a745a32eabb08f66f30fb8267c453.note: Q37 diet LPP. The scheme reprints the whole case study; the band keeps Figure-1 (food pyramid) and Figure-2 (the shaded feasible region) with their captions and drops the prose.

b6b41c4d1e57cf7d057bd8f6f4a46f6cabcc8f90.note: Q20 assertion-reason. Band drops the Assertion and Reason sentences, which are already stored as the stem, and keeps the graph with N(0,60), T(120,60), R, S, P, Q. ba113a7b0abc38e68365ddf51a82d5a76b1a064c.note: Q35(i). The note describes 'a capacitor network drawn between a terminal A on the left and B on the right, containing SIX capacitors, every one labelled C' — candidate [1]. Candidate [2] on the same page is Q35(iii)(b)'s dielectric slab.

The note describes 'a rectangle split by a vertical line into a left region hatched with diagonal lines labelled 2K and a right region hatched with horizontal lines labelled K, a dimension line beneath' — candidate [2]. Its page-mate [1] is Q35(i)'s capacitor network; the two sub-parts need DIFFERENT figures, which is why neither could be resolved automatically.

3bd58249d9a32c7576beac3eea77b98cc01dd757.note: Q30(iv)(b). The note says the INPUT signal and the CIRCUIT are both drawn AND 'all FOUR OPTIONS are themselves drawn waveforms', so the question is one visual block and the union of p20's five regions is the figure — the square-wave input plus diode/R_L circuit, then the four option waveforms. Union is safe here precisely because every region on the page belongs to this one question.

2ae27f0419416f0c3a8fcacc4bedf0a7380ef6be.note: Q11. The note says 'the four options ARE four drawn graphs and the printed paper gives them no text at all', and p8's four regions are exactly those four binding-energy curves. Union, for the same reason as 3bd58249: the whole page's figure content is this question's.

a3e40b79cc7cfa9a8cd3aec864385a42fff4e332.note: Q23(b) Biot-Savart at P(4,5). Page 16 carries TWO questions' figures, so the one-region rule refuses it and union would splice Q24's coils onto Q23's axes. Region [1] is the upper block (y 201-316pt): the x'-x / y-y' axis cross with z dashed to the lower left, a current arrow along +x on the x-axis, a current arrow along +y on the y-axis, and the point P marked (4, 5) in the first quadrant. Verified by rendering p16 and looking at it. The two current SENSES exist only here and both the magnitude and the direction of the resultant depend on them.

3189d1141af3ad17d33da2f0c2199f1d72cf4305.note: Q24 induced-current directions. Same page as Q23 and the same refusal; region [2] is the lower block (y 389-498pt): coil 2 on the left with terminals M and N, a variable resistor R2 and a cell in its circuit, facing coil 1 on the right with terminals O and P and resistor R1 and no source. Verified by rendering p16 and looking at it. The winding sense of each coil and the terminal labels exist ONLY in this drawing, and every one of the three sub-part answers is a direction. padTop=15 is measured off the rendered page's INK, not off the layout boxes: the stem's last prose line inks 360.4-371.6pt (descenders), the captions ink 375.2-383.8 and the drawing starts at 388.8, so a top edge at 373.7 clears the descenders by 2.1pt and the caption by 1.5. Reading the line BOXES instead would have put it at 372.5 and caught the descender tips.

9a6687222eaae15272226b5b9ed04376bf1c7871.note: Q29(iii): the two halves of a lens cut PERPENDICULAR to the axis, put back in contact. Page 16 carries this figure and Q29(iv)(a)'s, so the one-region rule refuses both and a union would splice them together. Region [1] is the upper block (y 340-416pt): a horizontal principal axis with the two plano-convex halves face to face on it, curved surfaces outwards. The arrangement IS the question, since the stem says only 'as shown in the figure'. The band is [0,1], the WHOLE region: it is there to switch PAD off. Measured on this page, 6pt of padding reaches the prose line above and the option row below, and both showed up sliced through the middle of the first crop. The region's own bounds are already clean on every side.

e85d7a7f01e587c7f815767451709cc9a7646828.note: Q29(iv)(a): the two halves of a lens cut ALONG the principal axis. Same page, same refusal; region [2] is the lower block (y 540-582pt): a horizontal line carrying the two half-lenses one AFTER the other, so light along the axis passes through both in succession and the powers add. That ordering is what decides the answer and it is nowhere in the stem. The band is [0,1], the WHOLE region: it is there to switch PAD off. Measured on this page, 6pt of padding reaches the prose line above and the option row below, and both showed up sliced through the middle of the first crop. The region's own bounds are already clean on every side.

_why_ms: The 2024 QUESTION PAPERS store the lower slices of every figure as corrupt data: content repeated 3x horizontally with the remainder black. It is in the source bytes, not the renderer - the extracted PNG is corrupt too - and it is uniform across a series, so no sibling paper rescues it (all three members measure 0.39-0.55 black). The 2024 MARKING SCHEMES reprint the same figures cleanly (0.00 black), so they are the source of record for these.
